concepts/land-as-commons.md.sentence: Barnes defines commons assets as "gifts" that are "shared" and for which we have a "joint obligation to preserve" them for future generations (Barnes 2006, Ch. 1).

concepts/land-as-commons.md.sentence: His proposed institutional innovation is the **commons trust** — a "market-based legal entity with the power to limit use of scarce commons, charge rent, and pay dividends — in both cash and services — to everyone" (Barnes 2006, p. 2).

concepts/land-as-commons.md.sentence: Barnes's framework reframes the "tragedy of the commons" as a pair of failures: "a tragedy of the market, which has no way of curbing its own excesses, and second a tragedy of government, which fails to protect the atmosphere because polluting corporations are powerful and future generations don't vote" (Barnes 2006, Ch. 1).

concepts/land-as-commons.md.name: Peter Barnes
concepts/land-as-commons.md.sentence: The commons trust is his remedy: by assigning property rights in common assets to trusts on behalf of future generations, the commons gains institutional defenders that, on Barnes’s account, government alone cannot reliably provide.
